en: Writes the m/z and RT windows of the expected products as a CSV in the columns of the inclusion list of mzFinder, sorted by RT; it adds no level and no verdict.

label: Adducts
it: Adducts of the ion table separated by commas, or a list of your own as a CSV with the header name;delta;charge;comment; one row per product and adduct; left empty it is [M-H]- for products linked in negative mode and [M+H]+ otherwise
en: Adducts of the ion table separated by commas, or a list of your own as a CSV with the header name;delta;charge;comment; one row per product and adduct; left empty it is [M-H]- for products linked in negative mode and [M+H]+ otherwise

label: RT half window
it: Each row spans the expected RT of the product plus and minus this; the start is never below 0
en: Each row spans the expected RT of the product plus and minus this; the start is never below 0

label: Export table as mzTab-M
it: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as an mzTab-M 2.0 file: one small molecule and one feature per row, areas per file and per group, and an evidence for a row whose identity names a hypothesis. Every row is reliability 4 (unknown compound): the export adds no identity and raises no level.
en: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as an mzTab-M 2.0 file: one small molecule and one feature per row, areas per file and per group, and an evidence for a row whose identity names a hypothesis. Every row is reliability 4 (unknown compound): the export adds no identity and raises no level.

label: Export table as CSV
it: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as a CSV file; the column names carry the file names, so equal names give equal bytes.
en: Writes the feature table, under the view of the filter step when one is wired, as a CSV file; the column names carry the file names, so equal names give equal bytes.

label: Format
it: full: one row per feature with the summaries; full_mzmine: the same with the words of mzmine for the filled and targeted cells; quant: the areas for FBMN; csv_semicolon: the sheet of features with ;
en: full: one row per feature with the summaries; full_mzmine: the same with the words of mzmine for the filled and targeted cells; quant: the areas for FBMN; csv_semicolon: the sheet of features with ;

label: Align features
it: Groups the features of all the files into rows by m/z and RT and writes the aligned table. Today one call (series::align_and_fill) does this and the filling of the gaps.
en: Groups the features of all the files into rows by m/z and RT and writes the aligned table. Today one call (series::align_and_fill) does this and the filling of the gaps.

label: Family link RT
it: Family mode: largest RT distance between an ion and the root of its family in one file for the two rows to be joined
en: Family mode: largest RT distance between an ion and the root of its family in one file for the two rows to be joined

label: Family link files
it: Family mode: an ion that is mostly the base of its own family joins a family only if it follows its root in this many files
en: Family mode: an ion that is mostly the base of its own family joins a family only if it follows its root in this many files

label: Coarse RT gap
it: RT gap of the coarse alignment that finds the anchors, and the widest spread of an anchor over the files: the drift between files the correction can follow
en: RT gap of the coarse alignment that finds the anchors, and the widest spread of an anchor over the files: the drift between files the correction can follow

label: RT correction
it: Brings the RT of every file to a common one before the features are grouped, from anchors (peaks every file shows) found by a coarse alignment: piecewise (medians by blocks), loess (local regression), ransac (a line robust to wrong anchors); off: the RT as the files give it
en: Brings the RT of every file to a common one before the features are grouped, from anchors (peaks every file shows) found by a coarse alignment: piecewise (medians by blocks), loess (local regression), ransac (a line robust to wrong anchors); off: the RT as the files give it

label: Weak tier files
it: Features from 0.3 of the minimum height up are kept as rows only if this many files in a run show them; 0 = no weak tier
en: Features from 0.3 of the minimum height up are kept as rows only if this many files in a run show them; 0 = no weak tier

label: Detect features
it: Finds the chromatographic peaks of the MS1 scans of each file, with their quality, isotopologues and families. The parameters are common to every algorithm; each algorithm adds its own.
en: Finds the chromatographic peaks of the MS1 scans of each file, with their quality, isotopologues and families. The parameters are common to every algorithm; each algorithm adds its own.

label: Long trace
it: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken
en: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

label: Mass defect
it: Unit axis only: fractional part of m/z where the strong peaks pile up; measured on the file when left empty
en: Unit axis only: fractional part of m/z where the strong peaks pile up; measured on the file when left empty

label: Merge overlap
it: Rows within the mass tolerance are one ion when their scans overlap by this share of the shorter trace
en: Rows within the mass tolerance are one ion when their scans overlap by this share of the shorter trace

label: RT range
it: Optional [min, max]: only rows eluting inside are kept, for every file; left empty, all rows
en: Optional [min, max]: only rows eluting inside are kept, for every file; left empty, all rows

label: Estimate parameters
it: Measures the noise floor, the m/z tolerance, the peak width and the dead time of each file from its own data and writes the proofs; it proposes values, the next step decides.
en: Measures the noise floor, the m/z tolerance, the peak width and the dead time of each file from its own data and writes the proofs; it proposes values, the next step decides.

label: Fill gaps
it: Where a file shows no feature of a row, integrates its raw trace in the window of the row and marks the cell as filled.
en: Where a file shows no feature of a row, integrates its raw trace in the window of the row and marks the cell as filled.

label: Long trace
it: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken
en: A trace longer than this is background and is not taken

label: Group ions
it: Groups the rows of a per-ion table that are one compound: same RT, heights that correlate over the files, then isotope steps and ion species that give one neutral mass. Every row stays, with a group id; the edges can go to a molecular network.
en: Groups the rows of a per-ion table that are one compound: same RT, heights that correlate over the files, then isotope steps and ion species that give one neutral mass. Every row stays, with a group id; the edges can go to a molecular network.

label: Apex distance
it: Largest apex distance in the shared files, as a share of the wider peak width (CAMERA perfwhm)
en: Largest apex distance in the shared files, as a share of the wider peak width (CAMERA perfwhm)

label: Negative ion species
it: Comma-separated species searched in negative mode, among [M-H]- [M+Cl]- [M+HCOO]- [M+CH3COO]- [M-H-H2O]- [M-2H]2- [2M-H]- [2M+HCOO]-
en: Comma-separated species searched in negative mode, among [M-H]- [M+Cl]- [M+HCOO]- [M+CH3COO]- [M-H-H2O]- [M-2H]2- [2M-H]- [2M+HCOO]-

label: Positive ion species
it: Comma-separated species searched in positive mode, among [M+H]+ [M+Na]+ [M+NH4]+ [M+K]+ [M+H-H2O]+ [M+H-2H2O]+ [M+2H]2+ [M+H+Na]2+ [2M+H]+ [2M+Na]+ [2M+NH4]+
en: Comma-separated species searched in positive mode, among [M+H]+ [M+Na]+ [M+NH4]+ [M+K]+ [M+H-H2O]+ [M+H-2H2O]+ [M+2H]2+ [M+H+Na]2+ [2M+H]+ [2M+Na]+ [2M+NH4]+

label: Largest charge
it: Largest charge an isotope step is read with
en: Largest charge an isotope step is read with

label: Link MS2 scans
it: Attaches to each peak the MS2 scans whose precursor lies in the peak and in the isolation window, with the purity of the precursor. Today this runs inside `features.detect` (one pass over the index), so it has no executor of its own: taking it out would change the bytes of the feature files.
en: Attaches to each peak the MS2 scans whose precursor lies in the peak and in the isolation window, with the purity of the precursor. Today this runs inside `features.detect` (one pass over the index), so it has no executor of its own: taking it out would change the bytes of the feature files.

label: Trigger margin
it: Seconds added on each side of the feature RT range to pair MS2 scans, 0 meaning one MS1 cycle.
en: Seconds added on each side of the feature RT range to pair MS2 scans, 0 meaning one MS1 cycle.

label: m/z tolerance
it: Window of the peak in the MS1 scan of the precursor; at unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da
en: Window of the peak in the MS1 scan of the precursor; at unit resolution the engine reads a negative value as Da

label: Weak purity
it: Purity below which an MS2 is weak evidence; it is not dropped
en: Purity below which an MS2 is weak evidence; it is not dropped

label: Import raw files
it: Recognises each vendor file set with the reader that accepts it and checks it against the limits of the platform; it changes nothing.
en: Recognises each vendor file set with the reader that accepts it and checks it against the limits of the platform; it changes nothing.

label: Working memory
it: Bytes of peaks held in memory while the index is built; the rest goes to a scratch file and the bytes of the index do not change
en: Bytes of peaks held in memory while the index is built; the rest goes to a scratch file and the bytes of the index do not change

label: Correct drift
it: Brings the areas of each batch to the level of the QC files along the order of injection; refused with fewer than 5 QC files in a batch or QC files that are not at the start and the end of it. The measured areas are never overwritten.
en: Brings the areas of each batch to the level of the QC files along the order of injection; refused with fewer than 5 QC files in a batch or QC files that are not at the start and the end of it. The measured areas are never overwritten.

label: Curve
it: Line or local line (LOESS) through the areas of the QC files of each batch, against the position of the injection
en: Line or local line (LOESS) through the areas of the QC files of each batch, against the position of the injection

label: LOESS span
it: Share of the QC files of a batch in the neighbourhood of each fit; used by the local line only
en: Share of the QC files of a batch in the neighbourhood of each fit; used by the local line only

label: Filter table
it: Keeps the rows that pass an ordered list of rules over the samples (campioni/2); blanks and dark files never count as samples, and a rule that cannot be evaluated is an error.
en: Keeps the rows that pass an ordered list of rules over the samples (campioni/2); blanks and dark files never count as samples, and a rule that cannot be evaluated is an error.

label: Keep the internal standard
it: The internal-standard row skips the blank rule, because it is spiked in the blanks too; needs the normalisation istd
en: The internal-standard row skips the blank rule, because it is spiked in the blanks too; needs the normalisation istd

label: Blank quantity
it: What is compared with the blank: area, height or normalised area; used with the sample to blank ratio only
en: What is compared with the blank: area, height or normalised area; used with the sample to blank ratio only

label: Sample to blank ratio
it: The largest area of a sample is at least this many times the mean area of the blanks; needs a blank in the samples; left empty, the rule is off
en: The largest area of a sample is at least this many times the mean area of the blanks; needs a blank in the samples; left empty, the rule is off

label: Blank comparison
it: max_feature judges the row by its best sample; each_feature keeps it only if every sample with a peak reaches the threshold
en: max_feature judges the row by its best sample; each_feature keeps it only if every sample with a peak reaches the threshold

label: Blank level
it: The blank level of a row: mean or maximum over the blank files (a blank without a peak counts as 0)
en: The blank level of a row: mean or maximum over the blank files (a blank without a peak counts as 0)

label: Subtract the blank
it: The view shows sample minus ratio times the blank level, not below 0, instead of only filtering; area or normalised area only; the ratio is at least 1 when any blank option is set
en: The view shows sample minus ratio times the blank level, not below 0, instead of only filtering; area or normalised area only; the ratio is at least 1 when any blank option is set

label: Duplicate m/z window
it: Of the rows within this many ppm in m/z and the duplicate RT window of each other only the one with the largest area is kept; left empty, the rule is off
en: Of the rows within this many ppm in m/z and the duplicate RT window of each other only the one with the largest area is kept; left empty, the rule is off

label: Duplicate RT window
it: RT distance under which two rows may be duplicates; used with the duplicate m/z window only
en: RT distance under which two rows may be duplicates; used with the duplicate m/z window only

label: Minimum files
it: Peaks found by the detection in at least this many files that are not blanks; left empty, the rule is off
en: Peaks found by the detection in at least this many files that are not blanks; left empty, the rule is off

label: Maximum QC CV
it: CV of the areas over the files with the role qc is at most this; a row needs a peak in at least the minimum number of them; fewer qc files than that is the error error.qc.tooFew; left empty, the rule is off
en: CV of the areas over the files with the role qc is at most this; a row needs a peak in at least the minimum number of them; fewer qc files than that is the error error.qc.tooFew; left empty, the rule is off

label: Minimum QC files
it: QC files with a peak that the row needs for the QC rule, and QC files that the series needs
en: QC files with a peak that the row needs for the QC rule, and QC files that the series needs

label: Count missing QC as 0
it: The QC CV counts the QC files without a peak as 0 and the row needs no minimum of them; the series still needs the minimum number of qc files
en: The QC CV counts the QC files without a peak as 0 and the row needs no minimum of them; the series still needs the minimum number of qc files

label: Kendrick mass defect
it: KM and KMD of every ion and the series of ions that share the KMD, with their members, steps and retention trend. A series is a candidate with its evidence, never an identification.
en: KM and KMD of every ion and the series of ions that share the KMD, with their members, steps and retention trend. A series is a candidate with its evidence, never an identification.

label: Explore with PCA
it: Principal components of the samples after the blank filter, the imputation and the scaling, with the variance explained and the stability of the loadings leaving one sample out; refused under 5 samples. A view: it tests nothing.
en: Principal components of the samples after the blank filter, the imputation and the scaling, with the variance explained and the stability of the loadings leaving one sample out; refused under 5 samples. A view: it tests nothing.

label: Components
it: Components kept in scores and loadings
en: Components kept in scores and loadings

label: Scaling
it: Pareto divides by the square root of the sd; auto divides by the sd and inflates the noise with few samples
en: Pareto divides by the square root of the sd; auto divides by the sd and inflates the noise with few samples

label: Plausibility of the values
it: Seven checks of the numbers the table shows: finite values, m/z and RT inside a real run, no negative area or height, a width and an apex for every detected peak, rows with no peak in any file and the ppm error of the identity columns. Numbers only: a flagged row is a value to look at, never a verdict.
en: Seven checks of the numbers the table shows: finite values, m/z and RT inside a real run, no negative area or height, a width and an apex for every detected peak, rows with no peak in any file and the ppm error of the identity columns. Numbers only: a flagged row is a value to look at, never a verdict.

label: Alignment tolerance
it: 0.1 Da or more is unit resolution and the ppm error is not read; without a value the recipe stored in the table decides
en: 0.1 Da or more is unit resolution and the ppm error is not read; without a value the recipe stored in the table decides

label: Largest ppm error
it: A row whose m/z is further than this from its neutral mass plus adduct is flagged; read only in a high-resolution table
en: A row whose m/z is further than this from its neutral mass plus adduct is flagged; read only in a high-resolution table

label: Compare conditions
it: Welch's t on log2(area + pseudocount) for each comparison of the design and a one-way ANOVA over all the conditions, with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and log2FC; refused with a reason and no number when a condition has fewer than 3 files. The p-values stay in this output: no view shows them.
en: Welch's t on log2(area + pseudocount) for each comparison of the design and a one-way ANOVA over all the conditions, with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and log2FC; refused with a reason and no number when a condition has fewer than 3 files. The p-values stay in this output: no view shows them.

label: Pseudocount
it: Added to every area before the logarithm and in the log2FC; without a value it is 3 x the median of the positive areas of the blanks, else of the reference, else the floor
en: Added to every area before the logarithm and in the log2FC; without a value it is 3 x the median of the positive areas of the blanks, else of the reference, else the floor

label: Aquatic hazard
it: One acute and one chronic aquatic hazard category per chemical identity, from versioned snapshots read from the campaign folder with their hash, no network. A hazard class is a property of a structure, not a risk: no concentration, no PNEC. A Level 3 identity carries the caveat of its candidate structure.
en: One acute and one chronic aquatic hazard category per chemical identity, from versioned snapshots read from the campaign folder with their hash, no network. A hazard class is a property of a structure, not a risk: no concentration, no PNEC. A Level 3 identity carries the caveat of its candidate structure.

label: Identification level
it: Gives each feature the level its evidence reaches (1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4, 5; 0 = detected, not annotated), with the basis and the reasons. Level 1 only with a standards file of yours; suspect fragments of screen.suspects give 3a. Level 2b is never given by the program: the chemist decides it. A CANOPUS class gives no level: it is a separate annotation.
en: Gives each feature the level its evidence reaches (1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4, 5; 0 = detected, not annotated), with the basis and the reasons. Level 1 only with a standards file of yours; suspect fragments of screen.suspects give 3a. Level 2b is never given by the program: the chemist decides it. A CANOPUS class gives no level: it is a separate annotation.

label: Class probability
it: A CANOPUS class is shown, as an annotation of its own that gives no level, at or above this probability
en: A CANOPUS class is shown, as an annotation of its own that gives no level, at or above this probability

label: COSMIC confidence
it: Confidence of the Level 3 gate; 0.64 is the threshold of the COSMIC paper, roughly an FDR of 10 %, a practical guide and no guarantee
en: Confidence of the Level 3 gate; 0.64 is the threshold of the COSMIC paper, roughly an FDR of 10 %, a practical guide and no guarantee

label: Conflicting libraries
it: best_match: the libraries are one library; level3: sources naming different structures give Level 3
en: best_match: the libraries are one library; level3: sources naming different structures give Level 3

label: Conflict margin
it: The best match keeps Level 2a only if its cosine exceeds the best match of a different structure by this much
en: The best match keeps Level 2a only if its cosine exceeds the best match of a different structure by this much

label: Standard MS2 score
it: Level 1: the MS2 score (entropy similarity, or cosine for a cosine hit) of the hit on the standard
en: Level 1: the MS2 score (entropy similarity, or cosine for a cosine hit) of the hit on the standard

label: Regulatory lists
it: Compares the identities with the regulatory package by InChIKey: the same full key is a match, the same first block a flagged match, a name or a formula never. A list entry says what a compound is on a list, nothing about this sample; no network.
en: Compares the identities with the regulatory package by InChIKey: the same full key is a match, the same first block a flagged match, a name or a formula never. A list entry says what a compound is on a list, nothing about this sample; no network.

label: Mass window
it: Entries of the lists outside this range of monoisotopic mass are left out; absent: all the entries
en: Entries of the lists outside this range of monoisotopic mass are left out; absent: all the entries

label: Formula from MS1
it: Candidate molecular formulas of each feature from the exact mass and, when the isotope finder finds a pattern, from the isotope pattern. The list is ordered by score and by a confidence that is a share of the list, never an identification: the chosen formula is the chemist's.
en: Candidate molecular formulas of each feature from the exact mass and, when the isotope finder finds a pattern, from the isotope pattern. The list is ordered by score and by a confidence that is a share of the list, never an identification: the chosen formula is the chemist's.

label: Elements
it: Ranges as C:0-50,H:0-100. Absent: C:0-50,H:0-100,N:0-8,O:0-15,P:0-2,S:0-3 plus the heavy elements the finder sees in the spectrum; the text given is searched as written
en: Ranges as C:0-50,H:0-100. Absent: C:0-50,H:0-100,N:0-8,O:0-15,P:0-2,S:0-3 plus the heavy elements the finder sees in the spectrum; the text given is searched as written

label: Charge
it: Absent: the isotope finder decides, and 1 when it finds no pattern; above 1 the formulas are those of the ion itself
en: Absent: the isotope finder decides, and 1 when it finds no pattern; above 1 the formulas are those of the ion itself

label: Formula from MS2
it: Assigns to each cleaned peak the closest sub-formula of the ion of the candidate formula and gives the neutral losses. A sub-formula supports the FORMULA, never the structure: isomers share it.
en: Assigns to each cleaned peak the closest sub-formula of the ion of the candidate formula and gives the neutral losses. A sub-formula supports the FORMULA, never the structure: isomers share it.

label: Sub-formula limit
it: Above this many sub-formulas the table is not built
en: Above this many sub-formulas the table is not built

label: Precursor tolerance
it: Precursor against the ion of the formula, the adduct with the smallest error of the polarity
en: Precursor against the ion of the formula, the adduct with the smallest error of the polarity

label: Retention time plausibility
it: Compares the retention time of a candidate with what the campaign's own confident identifications predict. A warning aid that ranks or doubts a candidate: it never applies a level and does not tell isomers apart.
en: Compares the retention time of a candidate with what the campaign's own confident identifications predict. A warning aid that ranks or doubts a candidate: it never applies a level and does not tell isomers apart.

label: Order
it: residual: within each query the candidates with the smallest |residual| first; a candidate without a prediction last
en: residual: within each query the candidates with the smallest |residual| first; a candidate without a prediction last

label: Parent RT
it: With a parent: the direction of the RT change (rt_dir) and whether it agrees with delta_logp (rt_dir_agrees)
en: With a parent: the direction of the RT change (rt_dir) and whether it agrees with delta_logp (rt_dir_agrees)

label: Find suspects
it: Searches the aligned feature table in the suspect lists you give by neutral mass for each adduct. Listed structures with the same formula are one isomer group, never one name. A regulatory package adds the lists naming each candidate. Candidates with their evidence, Level 5 (mass and formula) or 4 (also a candidate formula); no verdict.
en: Searches the aligned feature table in the suspect lists you give by neutral mass for each adduct. Listed structures with the same formula are one isomer group, never one name. A regulatory package adds the lists naming each candidate. Candidates with their evidence, Level 5 (mass and formula) or 4 (also a candidate formula); no verdict.

label: Regulatory lists
it: Ids of the lists of a regulatory package to screen, comma-separated; empty: every list in force
en: Ids of the lists of a regulatory package to screen, comma-separated; empty: every list in force

label: Handle chimeric MS2 spectra
it: Finds the other ions co-isolated in the precursor window of each MS2 spectrum, writes the purity of the precursor and the intruders, and leaves the spectrum as it is: the scores that read it discount the peaks an intruder can explain. Nothing is removed from the spectrum.
en: Finds the other ions co-isolated in the precursor window of each MS2 spectrum, writes the purity of the precursor and the intruders, and leaves the spectrum as it is: the scores that read it discount the peaks an intruder can explain. Nothing is removed from the spectrum.

label: In silico fragmentation
it: Breaks each candidate structure of a local list bond by bond and ranks it by the weight of the peaks its fragments explain. The candidates are a CSV list with PubChemLite columns, the structures of a screen.suspects result, or the in-silico package (PubChemLite, CC BY 4.0) downloaded once on a click and read by mass window. The result is a hypothesis with its proofs (peaks explained, mass error), never an identity. No network at analysis time.
en: Breaks each candidate structure of a local list bond by bond and ranks it by the weight of the peaks its fragments explain. The candidates are a CSV list with PubChemLite columns, the structures of a screen.suspects result, or the in-silico package (PubChemLite, CC BY 4.0) downloaded once on a click and read by mass window. The result is a hypothesis with its proofs (peaks explained, mass error), never an identity. No network at analysis time.

label: Score terms
it: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as the share of each explained peak and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change
en: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as the share of each explained peak and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Compare MS2 spectra
it: Scores each query MS2 spectrum against a spectral library inside the precursor window and keeps the best candidates per feature. A candidate is a hit with its scores and shared peaks, never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.
en: Scores each query MS2 spectrum against a spectral library inside the precursor window and keeps the best candidates per feature. A candidate is a hit with its scores and shared peaks, never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.

label: Library adduct contains
it: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library collision energy contains
it: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Decoys
it: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are
en: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are

label: Library instrument contains
it: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Matched peaks
it: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library name contains
it: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score
en: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score

label: Precursor window (low resolution)
it: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.
en: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: RT tolerance
it: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Score terms
it: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change
en: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Fragment tolerance (ppm)
it: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too
en: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too

label: Transition table
it: Matches each row of a table of SIM ions or SRM transitions to the chromatograms of each file at unit resolution and integrates the peak inside its RT window: area, height, apex RT, S/N and a flag when there is no peak. For rows without an RT it lists candidate peaks sorted by area; it never says which isomer a peak is.
en: Matches each row of a table of SIM ions or SRM transitions to the chromatograms of each file at unit resolution and integrates the peak inside its RT window: area, height, apex RT, S/N and a flag when there is no peak. For rows without an RT it lists candidate peaks sorted by area; it never says which isomer a peak is.

label: Peaks of the UV trace
it: Integrates the peaks of the UV/PDA trace of each file at one wavelength: apex, edges, width, height and area. With broad bands on it also finds the bands that the narrow peak finder loses. It lists peaks; it does not identify.
en: Integrates the peaks of the UV/PDA trace of each file at one wavelength: apex, edges, width, height and area. With broad bands on it also finds the bands that the narrow peak finder loses. It lists peaks; it does not identify.

label: Wavelength
it: The trace is the matrix at this wavelength; the nearest column when none is inside the band
en: The trace is the matrix at this wavelength; the nearest column when none is inside the band

label: Export annotations
it: Writes one CSV with, for every feature, the candidates of every identification method of the plan side by side (standard, library, in silico, suspect, formula), each with its own score and name, and the level and reason annot.level gave. It adds no identity and raises no level.
en: Writes one CSV with, for every feature, the candidates of every identification method of the plan side by side (standard, library, in silico, suspect, formula), each with its own score and name, and the level and reason annot.level gave. It adds no identity and raises no level.

label: Feature table
it: Indexes the files, detects the features of each, aligns them and writes the table as CSV: the chain of `mzlab-cli features` as one step.
en: Indexes the files, detects the features of each, aligns them and writes the table as CSV: the chain of `mzlab-cli features` as one step.

label: Compare algorithms
it: Runs the wrapped step once per variant on the same inputs and measures how the outputs differ; it does not say which variant is right.
en: Runs the wrapped step once per variant on the same inputs and measures how the outputs differ; it does not say which variant is right.

label: MSn graph as a figure
it: Draws the fragmentation graph as an SVG, a stand-alone HTML or a PNG: ions with m/z, relative intensity, MS levels and the proposed formulas, arrows for the neutral losses. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.
en: Draws the fragmentation graph as an SVG, a stand-alone HTML or a PNG: ions with m/z, relative intensity, MS levels and the proposed formulas, arrows for the neutral losses. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Format
it: svg: the static figure, colours written in the file; html: one file with no external resource, two views, data table and downloads; png: the SVG rasterised (only in a build with the cargo feature `png`)
en: svg: the static figure, colours written in the file; html: one file with no external resource, two views, data table and downloads; png: the SVG rasterised (only in a build with the cargo feature `png`)

label: View
it: tree: columns by MS level; radial: the precursor in the centre, one ring per step of the best path (the HTML has both and opens on this one)
en: tree: columns by MS level; radial: the precursor in the centre, one ring per step of the best path (the HTML has both and opens on this one)

label: MSn tree as a library
it: Writes the spectra of the fragmentation graph as an MSP or MassBank library, one record per spectrum of the tree, with the proposed formula and the neutral loss of each explained peak. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.
en: Writes the spectra of the fragmentation graph as an MSP or MassBank library, one record per spectrum of the tree, with the proposed formula and the neutral loss of each explained peak. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Annotate peaks
it: Write the sub-formula of each explained peak and the neutral loss from its precursor (MSP: quoted note; MassBank: PK$ANNOTATION and a COMMENT)
en: Write the sub-formula of each explained peak and the neutral loss from its precursor (MSP: quoted note; MassBank: PK$ANNOTATION and a COMMENT)

label: MS levels
it: all: one record per spectrum of the tree, MS2 and deeper; ms2: only the spectra of the first fragmentation
en: all: one record per spectrum of the tree, MS2 and deeper; ms2: only the spectra of the first fragmentation

label: MSn graph as a table
it: Writes the fragmentation graph as CSV: its ions with the proposed sub-formulas, its modifications (neutral losses between ions) or its peaks. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.
en: Writes the fragmentation graph as CSV: its ions with the proposed sub-formulas, its modifications (neutral losses between ions) or its peaks. The formulas are candidates of the graph, not identifications.

label: Table
it: modifications: one row per neutral loss between two ions of the tree (mass, formula, ppm, measures); nodes: one row per ion with its proposed sub-formula; peaks: one row per peak of every spectrum with its node
en: modifications: one row per neutral loss between two ions of the tree (mass, formula, ppm, measures); nodes: one row per ion with its proposed sub-formula; peaks: one row per peak of every spectrum with its node

label: Mass accuracy
it: Measures the mass error of each file on ions that are known to be there (the lab background list, internal standards and standards of the user) and reports offset, spread, standards and warnings; with a model it also writes a copy of the feature table with its m/z corrected. Numbers only, no verdict.
en: Measures the mass error of each file on ions that are known to be there (the lab background list, internal standards and standards of the user) and reports offset, spread, standards and warnings; with a model it also writes a copy of the feature table with its m/z corrected. Numbers only, no verdict.

label: Check run order
it: Reads the sample table and reports, for each batch, the number of files of each role, the largest gap between two QC injections, the blanks and the distinct standard levels, with a warning for a gap above the limit, a batch without QC or blank, too few standard levels, and a missing or repeated injection order. It reports facts, never a verdict.
en: Reads the sample table and reports, for each batch, the number of files of each role, the largest gap between two QC injections, the blanks and the distinct standard levels, with a warning for a gap above the limit, a batch without QC or blank, too few standard levels, and a missing or repeated injection order. It reports facts, never a verdict.

label: Calibrate
it: Applies imported calibration curves (signal = slope x concentration + intercept) to the signal of the matched rows of the table; concentrations outside the linear range or below zero are flagged. The line is not fitted here.
en: Applies imported calibration curves (signal = slope x concentration + intercept) to the signal of the matched rows of the table; concentrations outside the linear range or below zero are flagged. The line is not fitted here.

label: Methods text
it: Writes the methods of a run in English from its run record: every step with its version, algorithm and parameters, and the version of mzLab. It states what was set, never a result.
en: Writes the methods of a run in English from its run record: every step with its version, algorithm and parameters, and the version of mzLab. It states what was set, never a result.

label: Centroid the spectra
it: Reduces every profile scan of an mzML to one point per peak with the centroider of the archive; centroid scans, chromatograms and a file with no profile scan are left as they are.
en: Reduces every profile scan of an mzML to one point per peak with the centroider of the archive; centroid scans, chromatograms and a file with no profile scan are left as they are.

label: Threshold
it: A peak is kept when it stands this many sigma over the background (Poisson Z for counts); left out, the value of the mode of the file
en: A peak is kept when it stands this many sigma over the background (Poisson Z for counts); left out, the value of the mode of the file

label: Find spectra in a library
it: Writes the entries of the library you declare that have a given name, formula, InChIKey, accession or precursor m/z, with their peaks untouched, so that the next steps can use them as queries. The library is always the one you supply: nothing is built in and nothing is searched online.
en: Writes the entries of the library you declare that have a given name, formula, InChIKey, accession or precursor m/z, with their peaks untouched, so that the next steps can use them as queries. The library is always the one you supply: nothing is built in and nothing is searched online.

label: Look up by
it: The field of the library entries that value is compared with; precursor_mz takes a number and the window ppm
en: The field of the library entries that value is compared with; precursor_mz takes a number and the window ppm

label: Whole name
it: By name: the name must be the whole value, not only contain it (any case); the other fields are always compared whole
en: By name: the name must be the whole value, not only contain it (any case); the other fields are always compared whole

label: Entries kept
it: The first entries in the order of the library; the rest are not written
en: The first entries in the order of the library; the rest are not written

label: MS2 spectra from mzML
it: Reads the MS2 scans of data-dependent runs and writes them as spectra with precursor m/z and intensity, charge, RT and scan number; given a feature table it keeps the scans of its features and names each spectrum with the feature id.
en: Reads the MS2 scans of data-dependent runs and writes them as spectra with precursor m/z and intensity, charge, RT and scan number; given a feature table it keeps the scans of its features and names each spectrum with the feature id.

label: Fragment correlation
it: With `dia_pseudo`: least Pearson correlation between the trace of a fragment and that of the precursor
en: With `dia_pseudo`: least Pearson correlation between the trace of a fragment and that of the precursor

label: Cycles per peak
it: With `dia_pseudo`: fewest cycles of the RT range of a feature; a feature with fewer has no spectrum
en: With `dia_pseudo`: fewest cycles of the RT range of a feature; a feature with fewer has no spectrum

label: DIA pseudo spectra
it: For data-independent runs (SWATH, MSE): one pseudo MS2 spectrum per feature of the table, made of the fragments whose trace follows that of the precursor; needs the feature table, and the DDA scans are not written
en: For data-independent runs (SWATH, MSE): one pseudo MS2 spectrum per feature of the table, made of the fragments whose trace follows that of the precursor; needs the feature table, and the DDA scans are not written

label: Largest isolation window
it: Scans whose isolation window is wider are dropped; off when absent, and a scan that does not say its window is kept
en: Scans whose isolation window is wider are dropped; off when absent, and a scan that does not say its window is kept

label: MSn fragmentation graph
it: Merges the MSn spectra of an infusion into one graph of ions and neutral losses, with the sub-formulas of the fragments when the ion of the root is given. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.
en: Merges the MSn spectra of an infusion into one graph of ions and neutral losses, with the sub-formulas of the fragments when the ion of the root is given. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.

label: Trap cut-off q
it: Fragments below q/0.908 of the precursor m/z are treated as not observable.
en: Fragments below q/0.908 of the precursor m/z are treated as not observable.

label: Node to cleave
it: Node (nK) whose m/z is explained by structure cleavages; all for all nodes of level 2 or more.
en: Node (nK) whose m/z is explained by structure cleavages; all for all nodes of level 2 or more.

label: Compare the MS2 of the table rows
it: Takes the MS2 spectrum of every row of the aligned table, as the MGF export does, and scores it against a spectral library like spectra.match: the candidates of each row carry the score, the shared peaks, the decoy q-value and the name. A candidate is never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.
en: Takes the MS2 spectrum of every row of the aligned table, as the MGF export does, and scores it against a spectral library like spectra.match: the candidates of each row carry the score, the shared peaks, the decoy q-value and the name. label: Library adduct contains
it: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Library collision energy contains
it: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Decoys
it: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are
en: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are

label: Library instrument contains
it: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Matched peaks
it: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Take out the blank background
it: On: the MS2 peaks that recur in the blank files are taken out of every row, never the precursor; without a blank file nothing is taken out
en: On: the MS2 peaks that recur in the blank files are taken out of every row, never the precursor; without a blank file nothing is taken out

label: Spectrum of a row
it: best: the scan with the highest TIC of the file that has the best MS2 of the row; consensus: all the fitting scans of the row, merged across the files where it has a peak
en: best: the scan with the highest TIC of the file that has the best MS2 of the row; consensus: all the fitting scans of the row, merged across the files where it has a peak

label: Library name contains
it: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score
en: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score

label: Precursor window (low resolution)
it: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.
en: Precursor window in Da for unit-resolution data; 0 keeps the ppm window, or 0.7 Da for a unit-resolution file.

label: RT tolerance
it: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm
en: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm

label: Score terms
it: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change
en: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

label: Fragment tolerance (ppm)
it: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too
en: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search uses it too

label: Dig the unit-resolution series
it: Scores the products a parent can form in a series at unit resolution: peaks checked on their XIC, persistence, growth, blanks, chance. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.
en: Scores the products a parent can form in a series at unit resolution: peaks checked on their XIC, persistence, growth, blanks, chance. It proposes candidates; it does not identify.

label: Draw a structure
it: Opens the structure editor (Ketcher, in a sandboxed frame inside the page) so the student draws the parent or a product. A partial structure carries a Δ in a bracket or an attachment on any atom of a ring, which makes it a level 3 candidate and never an identification.
en: Opens the structure editor (Ketcher, in a sandboxed frame inside the page) so the student draws the parent or a product. A partial structure carries a Δ in a bracket or an attachment on any atom of a ring, which makes it a level 3 candidate and never an identification.

label: Reactivity of the parent
it: Computes where the parent is most reactive toward an electrophilic radical (condensed Fukui function f(-) per atom and per class of C-H sites). The result is a prior shown beside the sites of tp.position and never decides one: the experiment does.
en: Computes where the parent is most reactive toward an electrophilic radical (condensed Fukui function f(-) per atom and per class of C-H sites). The result is a prior shown beside the sites of tp.position and never decides one: the experiment does.

label: Conformers
it: ETKDG conformers of the parent, lowest energy first; f(-) is also computed on the lowest ones to give its spread
en: ETKDG conformers of the parent, lowest energy first; f(-) is also computed on the lowest ones to give its spread

label: Form of the parent
it: none: the SMILES as written; ph7: the most probable charge form at pH 7 from a table of typical pKa
en: none: the SMILES as written; ph7: the most probable charge form at pH 7 from a table of typical pKa

label: Draw the modification
it: Chooses the simplest form that tells the truth about a product: the structure itself only when the position is a site, a multicenter bond when every candidate lies in one aromatic ring, otherwise a bracket around a zone or the whole parent. Never one structure per site. The page draws it over the coordinates of the parent that Ketcher gives; without them the structure becomes a bracket.
en: Chooses the simplest form that tells the truth about a product: the structure itself only when the position is a site, a multicenter bond when every candidate lies in one aromatic ring, otherwise a bracket around a zone or the whole parent. Never one structure per site. The page draws it over the coordinates of the parent that Ketcher gives; without them the structure becomes a bracket.

label: Filters of the products
it: Hides a row for the first filter it fails: F1 peak quality, F2 isotopologue of another row, F3 as strong in the controls as in the treated samples, F4 constant ratio to the parent (in-source fragment or adduct), F5 formula error beyond the tolerance of the file. Rows are marked, not deleted. The decoys (rule deltas shifted by a mass defect) say how many matches are by chance.
en: Hides a row for the first filter it fails: F1 peak quality, F2 isotopologue of another row, F3 as strong in the controls as in the treated samples, F4 constant ratio to the parent (in-source fragment or adduct), F5 formula error beyond the tolerance of the file. Rows are marked, not deleted. The decoys (rule deltas shifted by a mass defect) say how many matches are by chance.

label: Lowest formula tolerance
it: Floor of the tolerance of a formula; the tolerance of a file is its measured error, kept between the two
en: Floor of the tolerance of a formula; the tolerance of a file is its measured error, kept between the two

label: Hypotheses of the products
it: Lists the ions that the chemistry says could be there, each with the source that proposed it: the parent times the photocatalytic rules (one or two steps), the offline suspect index, the expected members of the families already found, and lists the user typed or imported. One pass, fixed order, byte-identical on every run. A hypothesis is a place to look and what the search finds is graded afterwards.
en: Lists the ions that the chemistry says could be there, each with the source that proposed it: the parent times the photocatalytic rules (one or two steps), the offline suspect index, the expected members of the families already found, and lists the user typed or imported. One pass, fixed order, byte-identical on every run. A hypothesis is a place to look and what the search finds is graded afterwards.

label: Chained reactions
it: Most reactions chained from the parent; one hypothesis per net change of formula, the fewest steps first
en: Most reactions chained from the parent; one hypothesis per net change of formula, the fewest steps first

label: Most suspects
it: Hypotheses taken from the suspect index, the best supported first; the number left out is written in the registry
en: Hypotheses taken from the suspect index, the best supported first; the number left out is written in the registry

label: Unit resolution
it: Two formulas of the same nominal m/z and adduct are one hypothesis, the others its alternatives
en: Two formulas of the same nominal m/z and adduct are one hypothesis, the others its alternatives

label: Other polarity too
it: Expected members of a family in the other polarity too ([M-H]- of a positive base and the reverse)
en: Expected members of a family in the other polarity too ([M-H]- of a positive base and the reverse)

label: Link the MS2 of the products
it: Gives each row that passes the filters the modification it carries (formula change from the parent and isotope check of the MS1 at the apex), every DDA MS2 of its series with the purity of the isolation, and the comparison of the fragments with the MS2 and the MSn tree of the parent. Evidence for the chemist: it never names the product.
en: Gives each row that passes the filters the modification it carries (formula change from the parent and isotope check of the MS1 at the apex), every DDA MS2 of its series with the purity of the isolation, and the comparison of the fragments with the MS2 and the MSn tree of the parent. Evidence for the chemist: it never names the product.

label: Formula tolerance
it: Tolerance of the modification (neutral formula change) and of the comparison of the fragments with the parent
en: Tolerance of the modification (neutral formula change) and of the comparison of the fragments with the parent

label: Polarity
it: Polarity of the series: the adduct of the parent and the MS1 scans read for the purity
en: Polarity of the series: the adduct of the parent and the MS1 scans read for the purity

label: Lowest purity
it: A scan below this purity is chimeric and does not vote
en: A scan below this purity is chimeric and does not vote

label: Isolation centre
it: An MS2 scan belongs to a row when its isolation centre is within this many ppm of the m/z of the row
en: An MS2 scan belongs to a row when its isolation centre is within this many ppm of the m/z of the row

label: Network of the products
it: Draws the parent and the accepted products in columns by the number of steps from the parent, with an arc wherever a rule of the transformation table takes the ion formula of one to that of another. The source of an arc is the product that peaks first; an arc from the parent carries the fragments of the MS2 that are equal or shifted by the change. A network is evidence of kinship and never an identification: it raises no level.
en: Draws the parent and the accepted products in columns by the number of steps from the parent, with an arc wherever a rule of the transformation table takes the ion formula of one to that of another. The source of an arc is the product that peaks first; an arc from the parent carries the fragments of the MS2 that are equal or shifted by the change. A network is evidence of kinship and never an identification: it raises no level.

label: Fewest shared fragments
it: An arc from the parent whose MS2 was compared is kept with at least this many fragments in common, equal or shifted; 0 keeps every arc
en: An arc from the parent whose MS2 was compared is kept with at least this many fragments in common, equal or shifted; 0 keeps every arc

label: Position of the modification
it: Says which classes of sites of the parent the MS2 of a product is compatible with, never which site it is: classes are excluded, supported or undistinguished, the sublevel is 3a only when at least one class is excluded and at most three remain, and the rest is 3b. The reactivity of the parent is shown beside as a prior and does not decide.
en: Says which classes of sites of the parent the MS2 of a product is compatible with, never which site it is: classes are excluded, supported or undistinguished, the sublevel is 3a only when at least one class is excluded and at most three remain, and the rest is 3b. The reactivity of the parent is shown beside as a prior and does not decide.

label: Margin of the lead
it: Log-likelihood units a class must lead the second by to be called alone: two fragments' worth of evidence
en: Log-likelihood units a class must lead the second by to be called alone: two fragments' worth of evidence

label: Decide the levels
it: Keeps what the chemist decides for each row: a level, a note of up to 200 characters, or not a TP. The programme proposes and shows the evidence; a decision is allowed by the rules of the levels (2b only on a row proposed at 2a, 3a, 3b or 4; 1 only with a standard marked) and a refused one is listed with its reason and not counted. It decides nothing by itself.
en: Keeps what the chemist decides for each row: a level, a note of up to 200 characters, or not a TP. The programme proposes and shows the evidence; a decision is allowed by the rules of the levels (2b only on a row proposed at 2a, 3a, 3b or 4; 1 only with a standard marked) and a refused one is listed with its reason and not counted. It decides nothing by itself.

label: Convert to mzML
it: Writes the spectra of each sample as mzML; the version of this step names the writer.
en: Writes the spectra of each sample as mzML; the version of this step names the writer.

label: Compression level
it: zlib level of the binary arrays, 0 (none) to 9 (smallest)
en: zlib level of the binary arrays, 0 (none) to 9 (smallest)

label: Family row span
it: Family mode: largest RT span of the groups joined in one row
en: Family mode: largest RT span of the groups joined in one row

label: Rows
it: One row per family of ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) or one per ion
en: One row per family of ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) or one per ion

en: Largest gap of RT between neighbouring features of one row

en: Largest distance of an anchor from the line to agree with it (ransac)

en: Fraction of the anchors each local fit takes (loess)

en: A row with two features of one file (close isomers) is cut at the RT gaps above this

en: Unit axis only; left empty, the recipe of the file (measured window or 0.35 Da)

en: A feature whose apex is below this many times the noise of its flanks is dropped; 0 = off

it: Drops features narrower than this share of the typical peak width of the file; 0 = off
en: Drops features narrower than this share of the typical peak width of the file; 0 = off

it: 1 positive, -1 negative, 0 all MS1 scans
